datasets.title: Flood impact assessment in Sao Vicente Island, Cabo Verde (13 to 16 August 2025)
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20250812CPV This map illustrates satellite-detected mudflow extent in Sao Vicente Island, Cabo Verde as observed from Pleiades very high-resolution satellite image acquired on 13 to 16 August 2025. Within the analyzed area of approximately 270 km², about 12 km² of land appears to be affected by flood. Based on WorldPop population data and the flood extent, approximately 12,600 people are potentially exposed or living close to the flooded areas. Additionally, UNOSAT identified around 4,000 damaged buildings, five damaged bridges, and approximately 80 km of affected roads. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/flood-impact-assessment-in-sao-vicente-island-cabo-verde-13-to-16-august-2025]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts interpreted Pleiades very high-resolution satellite imagery acquired 13-16 August 2025 to delineate mudflow and flood extent across approximately 270 km² in Sao Vicente Island. Detected flood areas were overlaid with WorldPop population data to estimate exposed population, and building damage was assessed through visual change detection between pre- and post-event imagery.
